purpose: Three educational links from a historical map to existing people-level profiles; no present territorial or governmental equivalence is asserted.

inspection.scope: Viewed the actual supplied full-frame image at original detail. Read Nasaw in the large central-right circle, Cherrikies in the upper-right circle, and Chickisa in the far-right circle. No image alteration or inferred unlabeled people.
inspection.transcriptionNote: Nasaw is a modern transcription of the historical lettering; the long-s resembles f. The historical spellings Cherrikies and Chickisa are retained as map labels, not current preferred names.
inspection.catalogueRead: Read the existing historical-maps.json Catawba record and the earlier historical-maps-north-20261021.json notes. Their October 21 image-unviewed statement records an earlier inspection state; this supplied image was viewed October 22.
inspection.provenanceLimit: The image bears a small British Museum Add. MS. 4723 label. Its exact digital-file provenance and identity as a particular later photographic reproduction were not established. Do not silently describe these supplied pixels as the LOC 1929 photostat.

context.period: Underlying Indigenous draught presented around 1721; surviving colonial copies and later reproductions.
context.dateAndCopyingNote: LOC's guide distinguishes presentation around 1721 from its 1929 color photostat, catalogued under a 1724 call number. The supplied image should therefore not be described as an intact original 1721 deerskin or as made in 1929 without identifying its reproduction.
context.authorshipNote: Maker identity remains uncertain. LOC's guide allows Catawba or Cherokee attribution; its 2016 article says Catawba authorship is believed. Representation of a people on the map does not establish that people's authorship.
context.interpretationNote: The explanations emphasize relationships and routes. Circle size, adjacency, and connecting lines do not supply surveyed borders or a uniform geographic scale.

sourcesInspected.title: Celebrating Native American Cartography: The Catawba Deerskin Map
sourcesInspected.author: Tim St. Onge
sourcesInspected.scope: Read the complete article body, excluding reader comments: copying history, Nasaw identification, orientation, and network interpretation. Web lines 200–219 at inspection.
sourcesInspected.limit: Archive interpretation rather than a named Indigenous maker's testimony. Reader-comment authorship claims were excluded.

sourcesInspected.title: Historic Maps in K–12 Classrooms — Map 2 Curator's Notes
sourcesInspected.scope: Complete curator text read, especially upper-right circles and scale; lines 3–10.
sourcesInspected.limit: Maker attribution is stronger than LOC's; retain uncertainty.

sourcesInspected.title: Native American Spaces — Featured Selection of Maps, section 2
sourcesInspected.publicationDateNote: Guide displays last updated July 21, 2025; this is not the map's creation date.
sourcesInspected.scope: Read section 2 on the Catawba deerskin map, including its reproduction description and uncertain maker attribution. Web lines 16–23 at inspection.
sourcesInspected.limit: The direct item record at https://www.loc.gov/item/2005625337/ returned 403 on October 22; no new direct-item inspection is claimed.

associations.name: Catawba
associations.period: Network represented around 1721; surviving copy/reproduction history differs.
associations.relevance: Nasaw occupies the largest central circle. LOC identifies it as a central Catawba community, making this an educational link to Catawba history and relationships rather than proof of the maker's identity.
associations.observedLocation: Largest circle near the center-right; also named in the path inscription below-left.

evidence.pageReference: Paragraph beginning The map is a stylistic representation; web lines 212–213.
evidence.passageSummary: Explicitly identifies Nasaw as a central community of the Catawba Nation and describes the path inscription.

associations.inspectionScope: Actual supplied label plus archive explanation of the named community.
associations.uncertainty: Nasaw denotes a particular historical community; this link neither equates it with every Catawba community nor identifies the anonymous maker.

associations.name: Cherokee
associations.relevance: Cherrikies appears in the upper-right circle. Newberry explicitly identifies Cherokee among these represented communities. The link concerns historical representation.

evidence.pageReference: Curator's Notes, paragraph The headman also emphasized; line 9.
evidence.passageSummary: Identifies Cherokee and Chickasaw among upper-right circles.

associations.uncertainty: No present government, borders, or authorship determined.

associations.name: Chickasaw
associations.relevance: Chickisa appears in the far-right circle. Newberry explicitly identifies Chickasaw among these represented communities. The link concerns historical representation.

evidence.passageSummary: Identifies Chickasaw; adjacent discussion warns about uneven scale.

associations.uncertainty: No specific town, present jurisdiction, or authorship determined.

excludedInferences: No additional peoples identified from unlabeled circles, resemblance, or modern state location.
No exact modern coordinates, territorial polygons, land-title conclusions, or universal political alliances derived.
No attribution of authorship to Cherokee merely because its name appears; no definite Catawba maker inferred from the conventional map title.
No source-count or research-depth promotion for destination profiles; these are map relationships only.
unresolved: Precise provenance of the owner-supplied digital reproduction remains unverified; archival subject identification is stronger than file-level provenance.
Other historical map labels were outside this three-association pass.
